sources.title: Relative Survival Modeling for Appraising the Cost-Effectiveness of Life-Extending Treatments: An Application to Tafamidis for ATTR-CM

terms.rationale: Europe PMC deposits the article as CC BY-NC; bounded research-only derived method facts are permitted with attribution. No article bytes or substantial text are retained.

derived_method_facts: Relative-survival models add an independently modelled excess hazard to externally defined expected mortality.
Candidate extrapolations included exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, log-logistic, lognormal, generalized gamma, and gamma forms.
Selection considered statistical fit, empirical hazard shape, clinical plausibility, and validation against long-term extension observations through 72 months.
Country-specific life tables informed expected mortality; uncertainty in extrapolation remained material and alternative distributions produced different mean survival.
